title: Esports Enterprise, Brand, Audience & Ethics Atlas
description: Curriculum-first concept map for Pearson BTEC Level 3 Esports Units 3, 7, 10, 15 and 19, linking enterprise, branding, social media, audiences, ethics and immersive customer experience.

curriculumPresets.title: Full enterprise & audience system
curriculumPresets.description: Explore how esports organisations create value, build brands, reach audiences and manage ethical responsibilities.

curriculumPresets.title: L3 Unit 3: Enterprise & Entrepreneurship
curriculumPresets.description: Trace opportunity, value proposition, research, business models, revenue, costs, risk and measures of success.

curriculumPresets.title: L3 Unit 7: Branding
curriculumPresets.description: Connect identity, positioning, audience, visual language, touchpoints and brand consistency.

curriculumPresets.title: L3 Unit 10: Social Media Management
curriculumPresets.description: Follow audience segmentation through content strategy, engagement, moderation, conversion and analytics.

curriculumPresets.title: L3 Unit 15: Ethical & Current Issues
curriculumPresets.description: Explore toxicity, inclusion, advertising, commercial influence, digital choice architecture and responsible online practice.

curriculumPresets.title: L3 Unit 19: Customer Immersion Experiences
curriculumPresets.description: Map customer journeys, interaction, personalisation, accessibility, immersion and evaluation.

nodes.name: Esports Enterprise & Audience System
nodes.note: Esports enterprises connect value creation, audiences, brands, media, customer experience and ethical responsibilities.
nodes.hook: Choose one esports organisation and trace how it creates value without beginning with prize money.

nodes.name: Enterprise & Entrepreneurship
nodes.note: Enterprise turns an identified need or opportunity into a sustainable offer through resources, decisions and managed risk.
nodes.hook: Find an esports problem worth solving before inventing a product.

nodes.name: Opportunity Identification
nodes.note: An opportunity exists when a defined audience has an unmet or poorly served need that an organisation can address credibly.
nodes.hook: Distinguish a genuine opportunity from something the founder simply likes.

nodes.name: Market & Audience Research
nodes.note: Research reduces uncertainty by collecting evidence about customers, competitors, demand, behaviour and context.
nodes.hook: Combine one primary and one secondary source before making a market claim.

nodes.name: Value Proposition
nodes.note: A value proposition explains which audience problem is being solved and why the offer is preferable to alternatives.
nodes.hook: Write the value proposition without using adjectives such as amazing, innovative or unique.

nodes.name: Business Model
nodes.note: A business model describes how an organisation creates, delivers and captures value using partners, activities, resources, customers and revenue mechanisms.
nodes.hook: Explain who pays, what they receive and why the model remains viable when audiences fluctuate.

nodes.name: Revenue Streams
nodes.note: Esports revenue can come from sponsorship, advertising, media, merchandise, tickets, services, subscriptions, partnerships and other commercial activity.
nodes.hook: Rank three revenue streams by control, predictability and dependence on audience size.

nodes.name: Costs & Resources
nodes.note: Enterprises consume financial, human, technical and physical resources, with both fixed and variable costs affecting viability.
nodes.hook: Separate costs that remain even when no event runs from costs that scale with activity.

nodes.name: Enterprise Risk
nodes.note: Strategic, financial, operational, legal and reputational risks can prevent an enterprise from meeting its purpose.
nodes.hook: Pair every major risk with a realistic mitigation rather than writing avoid risk.

nodes.name: Measures of Success
nodes.note: Success measures should connect directly to enterprise purpose and may include financial, audience, service, brand or operational indicators.
nodes.hook: Choose one vanity metric and replace it with a measure that changes a decision.

nodes.name: Brand Strategy
nodes.note: A brand is the pattern of meanings and expectations associated with an organisation, shaped through identity, behaviour, communication and experience.
nodes.hook: Separate the brand itself from its logo.

nodes.name: Brand Identity
nodes.note: Identity includes the deliberate names, visual systems, voice and behaviours an organisation uses to present itself.
nodes.hook: Audit whether the same identity is recognisable across stream, social post, jersey and website.

nodes.name: Positioning
nodes.note: Positioning defines the space a brand aims to occupy in its audience's mind relative to alternatives.
nodes.hook: Plot two competing esports brands on axes that matter to their actual audiences.

nodes.name: Visual Language
nodes.note: Colour, typography, imagery, motion and composition create recognisable visual cues when applied consistently and accessibly.
nodes.hook: Identify which elements still communicate the brand after the logo is removed.

nodes.name: Brand Touchpoints
nodes.note: Every interaction with an organisation can reinforce or contradict its intended brand, including support, events, social media and products.
nodes.hook: Find a non-visual touchpoint that can damage an otherwise strong brand.

nodes.name: Social Media Strategy
nodes.note: Social-media strategy connects audience, objective, platform, content, moderation and measurement instead of treating posting frequency as the goal.
nodes.hook: Start with an objective and audience, then decide whether a platform is actually suitable.

nodes.name: Audience Segmentation
nodes.note: Segmentation groups audiences by meaningful characteristics, needs or behaviours so communication can be targeted appropriately.
nodes.hook: Create segments based on behaviour or need rather than only age and gender.

nodes.name: Content Strategy
nodes.note: Content strategy determines what will be communicated, in which formats, for which audience and purpose, across a planned cadence.
nodes.hook: Explain what job each content type performs rather than filling a calendar with random posts.

nodes.name: Engagement
nodes.note: Engagement measures audience interaction, but its meaning depends on the intended outcome and the platform behaviour generating it.
nodes.hook: Explain why a controversial post can have high engagement while damaging the organisation.

nodes.name: Conversion
nodes.note: A conversion occurs when an audience member completes a desired action such as registration, purchase, signup or attendance.
nodes.hook: Define one conversion event and the steps that must happen before it.

nodes.name: Social Analytics
nodes.note: Analytics turn reach, retention, engagement, click and conversion data into evidence for evaluating content and campaign choices.
nodes.hook: Choose a metric because it answers a question, not because the dashboard makes it prominent.

nodes.name: Community Moderation
nodes.note: Moderation applies community rules and interventions to protect participation, safety and organisational standards.
nodes.hook: Design a moderation ladder that distinguishes mistake, disruption and serious abuse.

nodes.name: Ethics & Current Issues
nodes.note: Ethical analysis examines who benefits, who may be harmed, what responsibilities exist and whether commercial or technological choices are justified.
nodes.hook: Analyse an issue using stakeholders and consequences before giving your own opinion.

nodes.name: Toxicity & Online Harms
nodes.note: Abusive, discriminatory or disruptive behaviour can exclude participants, damage wellbeing and undermine communities and competitions.
nodes.hook: Separate preventative design, moderation response and sanctioning as three different controls.

nodes.name: Inclusion & Representation
nodes.note: Inclusion concerns whether environments, systems and cultures enable meaningful participation across diverse users rather than merely displaying diversity.
nodes.hook: Find a barrier caused by process or design rather than individual attitude alone.

nodes.name: Commercialisation
nodes.note: Commercial investment can expand esports while also shaping schedules, content, incentives, access and organisational priorities.
nodes.hook: Identify one benefit and one potential conflict created by the same sponsor relationship.

nodes.name: Advertising Disclosure
nodes.note: Paid or commercially connected social content should be clearly recognisable as advertising so audiences are not misled about its purpose.
nodes.hook: Audit three creator posts and decide whether the commercial relationship is immediately clear.

nodes.name: Online Choice Architecture
nodes.note: Digital interfaces can shape decisions through ordering, defaults, urgency, friction and other design choices; some patterns can harm consumer choice.
nodes.hook: Find a design that makes one option easier than another and judge whether that influence is justified.

nodes.name: Children, Data & Online Design
nodes.note: Services likely to be accessed by children require particular care around data use, defaults, transparency and design choices.
nodes.hook: Review an esports signup flow from the perspective of a younger user rather than only the organiser.

nodes.name: Customer Immersion Experience
nodes.note: Immersive customer experience combines environment, interaction, narrative, technology and service design to create purposeful participation.
nodes.hook: Define the intended customer outcome before choosing VR, AR or any other technology.

nodes.name: Customer Journey
nodes.note: A customer journey maps stages and touchpoints before, during and after an experience to identify needs, friction and opportunities.
nodes.hook: Map discovery, arrival, participation and follow-up for an esports event.

nodes.name: Interaction Design
nodes.note: Interaction design determines how customers act, receive feedback and understand available choices within an experience.
nodes.hook: Remove one interaction that adds novelty but does not help the intended experience.

nodes.name: Personalisation
nodes.note: Personalisation adapts content or interaction to user characteristics or behaviour, creating value only when data use and relevance are justified.
nodes.hook: State what data is actually needed for the personalisation and what should not be collected.

nodes.name: Experience Evaluation
nodes.note: Evaluation compares intended outcomes with observation, feedback and behavioural evidence to judge whether the experience worked.
nodes.hook: Use completion, behaviour and feedback together rather than relying on did you enjoy it.
